A states this correctly and concludes that a teacher/pupil shortcut is inadmissible because no agreed full path exists; B states the opposite rule -- 'CRM deliberately does not declare shortcut properties for relations that are derivable from the primitive event pattern' -- which the Minimality text (crm732#s0053: classes and properties 'are either primitive, or they are key concepts in the practical scope') does not say and which P152, cited by B itself, refutes. better_modelling: Both stop one step short. P11 had participant is symmetric co-presence and its own scope note says it 'does not imply any causal relationship' (B quotes this), so forty P11 links record that the two men were in a room together forty times and nothing about who taught whom -- the exact fact the archive asked for is not recoverable from the chain either answer builds. The CRM's more specific terms are: (1) each session as E7 Activity, P2 has type 'tune-teaching session', with P14 carried out by the granduncle and P14.1 in the role of 'teacher' (E55) -- P14 (E7 -> E39, FOL P14(x,y,z) => [P14(x,y) & E55(z)]) exists precisely to specify 'the nature of an Actor's participation', and P11 for the grandnephew if responsibility is not asserted; (2) if the pair-relation itself must be a catalogue object, the standing CRMBase idiom is an E74 Group typed by relation with P107 has current or former member and P107.1 kind of member 'teacher'/'pupil' -- P107's own declaration gives 'married couple ... kind of member husband' and E74's scope note admits gatherings unified by 'actions performed together' and 'a common purpose such as study', and explicitly names married couples and family as E74 examples. Both answers reject E74 on unadopted 2014-2015 listserv opinion (Ore's 'not necessary' is not 'not permitted') without confronting the current scope note that arguably licenses it; (3) P15 was influenced by (E7 -> E1) is the declared construct for carrying transmission direction into the nephew's later performances, and neither answer mentions it.
reasoning: Both reach the same core modelling (forty distinct E7 Activity instances, both E21 Persons attached, relation inferred not asserted), and both are right that no person-to-person teaching property exists in the 241-item listing (verified) and that Issue 256 closed on 2017-10-10 deferring person-relations beyond CRMBase to a 'CRMsoc' that does not exist (verified; A missed this register-level closure and wrongly says there is 'no final SIG ruling'). Both are suboptimal for the same reason: they build the evidence chain out of P11 alone, whose scope note denies any causal implication, so the chain cannot express the direction the archive wants; P14 with P14.1 in the role of, and P107.1 kind of member on a typed E74, are the more specific declared terms and neither answer proposes them.
